slot.brief: Two stars orbiting their common centre of mass; relate orbital radii to masses and derive/find the orbital period or speed symbolically; multi-step gravitational reasoning.

stem: Two stars of masses $M$ and $3M$ orbit their common centre of mass in circles. If the lighter star's orbital radius is $R$, what is their orbital period?

verdicts.working: The separation is d=4R/3, since the lighter star is 3/4 of the separation from the centre of mass. Thus T=2π√[d³/(G·4M)]=(8π/(3√3))√(R³/GM), which is option B.

working:
$MR=3M(d-R)\Rightarrow d=\dfrac{4R}{3}$. $T=2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{d^3}{G(4M)}}=\dfrac{8\pi}{3\sqrt{3}}\sqrt{\dfrac{R^3}{GM}}$.

Independent check: The separation is d=4R/3, since the lighter star is 3/4 of the separation from the centre of mass. Thus T=2π√[d³/(G·4M)]=(8π/(3√3))√(R³/GM), which is option B.
solution:
The centre-of-mass condition gives $MR=3M(d-R)$, so $d=\dfrac{4R}{3}$. For a binary system, $T=2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{d^3}{G(4M)}}$.
$$T=2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{(4R/3)^3}{4GM}}=\dfrac{8\pi}{3\sqrt{3}}\sqrt{\dfrac{R^3}{GM}}$$
